title: SEC sweeps opening weekend for first time since 1997
dek: All 16 SEC teams won their season openers on September 3-5, marking the conference's first perfect opening weekend in 29 years. The conference faced only non-conference opponents, with ranked teams including #3 Georgia, #5 Texas, and #11 LSU winning decisively.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The SEC went 16-0 in Week 1 of 2026, the first time since 1997 when the conference had only 12 teams.
bottom_line: Conference play begins the week of September 15, when Oklahoma travels to Michigan and Texas to Ohio State, tests against Power Four opponents outside the SEC. The early dominance was built against non-conference teams; the real measure comes in September when SEC teams face ranked opponents from other conferences and begin their own internal schedule.
body:
All 16 SEC teams won their season openers on September 3-5, 2026, according to Yahoo Sports reporting. The conference's perfect Week 1 record marks the first time since 1997, when the SEC carried only 12 teams, that every conference member won its opening game.
The sweep spanned games across three days. Missouri defeated Arkansas-Pine Bluff 54-14 on September 3. On Friday, September 4, #10 Oklahoma defeated UTEP 51-0. Saturday, September 5 carried the bulk of the action: #13 Alabama defeated Eastern Carolina 48-10, South Carolina shut out Kent State 57-0, #3 Georgia defeated Tennessee State 63-3, Auburn edged Baylor 17-16, #20 Tennessee defeated Furman 56-9, #5 Texas defeated Texas State 59-7, Arkansas defeated North Alabama 31-14, #8 Texas A&M defeated Missouri State 50-0, Vanderbilt defeated Austin Peay 28-9, Mississippi State defeated UL Monroe 62-13, Florida defeated Florida Atlantic 66-21, #11 LSU defeated Clemson 51-10, and #9 Ole Miss defeated #24 Louisville 41-38. Kentucky completed the sweep earlier, defeating Youngstown State 45-13 in what Yahoo Sports reported as sweltering weather conditions.
The opening week showcased the conference against non-conference opponents. All 16 teams faced teams outside the SEC, with rankings reflecting preseason or early-season designations.
Next week brings SEC teams into higher-profile matchups.  Other upcoming SEC matchups include Missouri at Kansas, Oklahoma at Michigan, Texas A&M against Arizona State, Tennessee at Georgia Tech, and Texas at Ohio State, according to the reporting.
